question: Before carrying a passenger or heavy load, the manual recommends this be attempted only by:
choice_a: Experienced riders, due to the extra practice and caution required
choice_b: New riders, to build confidence quickly
choice_d: Riders who have never had a crash
explanation: The extra weight of a passenger or cargo affects handling significantly, so only experienced riders should attempt to carry passengers or large loads.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.38, 'Carrying Passengers and Cargo'

question: When preparing a motorcycle for a passenger or load, tire pressure should be checked on:
choice_a: The rear tire only, since it bears most of the weight
choice_b: Both tires, per the owner's manual specifications
choice_d: Neither tire, since pressure does not change with load
explanation: Check the air pressure of both tires, referring to the owner's manual or label; even though most added weight is on the rear, the front tire pressure matters too.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.38, 'Preparing Your Motorcycle'

question: A passenger should be told to get on the motorcycle only after:
choice_a: The rider has removed their own helmet
choice_c: The engine is started and the transmission is in neutral, with the rider's feet on the ground and brakes applied
explanation: The passenger should mount only after the engine is started and the transmission is in neutral, with the rider keeping both feet on the ground and brakes applied.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.38-39, 'Preparing Your Passenger to Ride'

question: Children carried as passengers should be positioned:
choice_a: In front of the rider, so the rider can watch them
choice_c: In a sidecar only, never on the main seat
explanation: Children should be placed immediately behind the rider; a child in front cannot properly balance and may interfere with the rider's control.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.38, 'Preparing Your Passenger to Ride'

question: Passengers should be instructed to lean:
choice_a: With the rider through turns and curves
choice_c: Only when instructed verbally each time
choice_d: Never; the passenger should stay perfectly rigid
explanation: The passenger should stay directly behind the rider and lean with the rider through turns and curves.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.39, 'Preparing Your Passenger to Ride'

question: With a passenger aboard, the motorcycle's response to rider inputs will be:
choice_b: Slower -- it takes longer to speed up, slow down, or turn
explanation: Your motorcycle will respond more slowly when riding with a passenger; the heavier the passenger, the longer it takes to speed up, slow down, or turn.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.40, 'Riding With Passengers'

question: When riding with passengers, the manual advises riders to:
choice_a: Ride faster to compensate for the added weight
choice_b: Maintain the same speed as when riding solo
choice_c: Ride a little slower, especially in curves, corners, or over bumps
choice_d: Follow more closely to conserve fuel
explanation: With passengers, ride a little slower, especially taking curves, corners, or bumps, since scraping the ground at lean angle can cause loss of steering control.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.40, 'Riding With Passengers'

question: When loading cargo, the manual recommends packing heavier items:
choice_a: As far to the rear of the motorcycle as possible
choice_c: On top of a sissy bar for visibility
choice_d: Over or in front of the rear axle, keeping the load forward
explanation: Keep the load forward, packing heavier items toward the front over or in front of the rear axle; loads mounted behind the rear axle can affect turning, braking, and cause wobble.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.39-40, 'Carrying Loads'

question: Attaching a load to a sissy bar is discouraged because it:
choice_a: Raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and can upset balance
explanation: Secure loads low or put them in saddlebags; attaching a load to a sissy bar raises the center of gravity and can upset the motorcycle's balance.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.40, 'Tips for Traveling with Passengers and Cargo'

question: When using saddlebags, the manual recommends loading each bag with:
choice_a: As much weight as physically possible
choice_b: About the same weight to avoid pulling the motorcycle to one side
choice_c: Only lightweight items in one bag and heavy items in the other
choice_d: Nothing; saddlebags should remain empty for balance
explanation: Load saddlebags with about the same weight; an uneven load can cause the motorcycle to pull to one side, and overloading may cause bags to catch in the wheel or chain.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.40, 'Tips for Traveling with Passengers and Cargo'

question: Before loading, the manual recommends checking headlight aim by:
choice_a: Relying on the dealership to verify aim once a year
choice_b: Only checking it after dark on the open road
choice_c: Marking the beam location on a wall about 10 feet away, then rechecking with a full load
choice_d: Assuming aim never changes with load
explanation: Position the motorcycle about 10 feet from a wall in an unlighted garage, mark the beam location with chalk, then recheck the beam location with a full load and passenger.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.38, 'Preparing Your Motorcycle'

question: A fully loaded motorcycle's performance compared to an unloaded one will typically show:
choice_b: Shorter stopping distances due to added weight
choice_d: Lower acceleration power and possibly increased stopping distances
explanation: A fully loaded motorcycle's power when accelerating will be lower, increasing passing times and distances, and braking may feel different with increased stopping distances.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.41, 'Pre-Ride Test'

question: According to the manual, when planning a loaded touring trip, riders should not exceed:
choice_a: The gross vehicle weight rating when traveling with cargo and a passenger
choice_b: Any weight limit, as motorcycles have no rating
choice_d: The weight of the motorcycle itself
explanation: Do not exceed gross vehicle weight rating when traveling with cargo and a passenger, and always adjust the motorcycle to compensate for the added weight.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.39, 'Carrying Loads'
